thread:
alex: @channel paging — Vectra (private VPC) reporting widespread 401s after last night's customer-managed cert rotation. Errors in their app: "JWT verification failed: unknown kid" and intermittent TLS handshake failures from our edge to their identity proxy. Customer impact: production inference failing for ~30% of requests. Can oncall triage?
incident-bot: Incident created: /incidents/INC-2026-427 (priority: P1) — paging oncall. PagerDuty notified.
oncall-bot: @maria you are oncall for incidents this shift — please acknowledge.
maria: acked. jumping in. alex, can you paste any logs or customer error samples?
alex: pasted below from Vectra error stream (redacted):
```
2026-03-15T03:12:07Z ERROR http: request failed tenant=vectra err="jwt verification failed: unknown kid=ae3f" route=/v1/generate
2026-03-15T03:12:08Z WARN tls: handshake failed remote=10.2.1.55:443 err="tls: client certificate expired"
```
maria: ok looks like two separate but related things: their OIDC provider rotated JWKS keys (kid mismatch) and their client certs for mTLS may have expired. first triage steps: 1) check if our VPC auth bridge cached the old jwks; 2) check if their jwks endpoint is returning expected keys; 3) see if our sidecar is rejecting expired client certs. i'll look at the bridge logs. jordan: can you open the customer's jwks URL and confirm? amina-cs, flag FYI to Vectra.
jordan: hitting their jwks endpoint now: `https://id.vectra.internal/.well-known/jwks.json` — i get a 200 but the returned list has only the new kid (be5b) — old kid (ae3f) is not present. that lines up with unknown kid.
amina-cs: pinged customer contacts (eng@vectra and infra@vectra). they confirm they rotated keys at 01:30 UTC and believed the rotation to be fully propagated. they also said they rotated client certs at the same time.
maria: thanks. two mitigation options: A) add short-term support for the new kid only and allow fallback for old kid by replaying requests with manual verification (risky); B) temporarily accept both new and previously cached keys by warming jwks cache from their old key if we have it; C) ask customer to reissue certs or rollback rotation. we need a solution with minimal blast radius.
ben-eng: quick note — our VPC auth bridge caches JWKS for 5m by default, but we also have a hot-cache fallback that can be seeded from last-known keys stored in customer metadata (if present). check `/etc/redwood/custom-jwks/vectra.json` on the bridge.
maria: i'm SSHing to the auth bridge in the vectra VPC now (jump via bastion). pulling file: `/etc/redwood/custom-jwks/vectra.json` — file exists and contains the old key! So we can seed the runtime cache with it. plan: seed the hot-cache with old kid, accept both ae3f and be5b for 15 minutes, then force re-eval with customer. will that keep us safe? jordan: yes, that should let in requests signed with the old key for a short window and buy time for the customer to validate client certs.
maria: executing cache-seed. command: 
```
ssh -J bastion@jump.prod redwood-auth-bridge-23 -- sudo cp /etc/redwood/custom-jwks/vectra.json /var/lib/authbridge/hotcache/vectra.jwks && sudo systemctl restart redwood-auth-bridge
```
maria: done. restarting bridge now. watching logs.
(2m later)
maria: logs show: `hotcache seeded for tenant=vectra keys=[ae3f,be5b] ttl=900s` — starting to see 200s for some previously failing requests.
alex: customer reporting partial recovery: ~70% success now. still seeing TLS client cert failures ~30%.
jordan: i pulled TLS logs from the bridge: some upstream connections show `certificate has expired` with client cert expiration=2026-03-15T01:10:00Z — yep their certs expired at rotation time.
amina-cs: customer confirms their cert rotation produced a new cert but their deployment rolled back for some hosts, leaving mixed cert fleet. they're rolling forward but expect a ~20–40 min window to fully propagate.
maria: mitigation path: 1) keep hot-cache seeded for 15min (already set); 2) add a temporary bypass route for legacy TLS behavior for vectra traffic (fall back to non-mTLS path) — that's higher risk but would cut impact quickly; 3) ask customer to complete rollout. what does security think about bypass? @sre-lead opinion?
sre-lead: bypassing mTLS for a tenant is a big no unless customer explicitly signs an exception and we can limit to specific IPs + short TTL. we can do it as emergency if customer requests it and confirms traffic is within controlled egress CIDRs.
maria: ok we'll avoid bypass unless Vectra signs it. continue hot-cache and monitor. amina-cs can you nudge customer to finish cert rollout and confirm when done? Also let's update status page for impacted region/tenant.
amina-cs: sent message asking them to prioritize cert rollout and to send their rollout completion timestamp. also asked for signed exception if they want mTLS bypass.
incident-bot: Update: mitigation applied — jwks hot-cache seeded. Impact reduced to ~30% requests failing. Monitoring in effect.
jordan: adding ephemeral alert for jwks key rotation detection to avoid silent breakage next time: rule: if jwks kid set changes and cached requests > 1% fail with unknown kid within 10m, page oncall.
maria: good. can we also add an event in customer's config to keep a cached snapshot of last 24h of jwks in S3? ben-eng: we already store a 72h rolling snapshot but it's not always auto-seeded. I'll add agent to auto-seed on detection of rotation.
alex: CS asked for a one-paragraph summary for the customer and timeline. i'll draft: "We detected a JWKS rotation at ~01:30 UTC which removed the previously used key (ae3f) from your JWKS endpoint. Our auth bridge cached the old key and we seeded the runtime hot-cache to accept both keys, restoring most traffic. Some clients had expired mTLS certs during your rollout causing TLS handshake failures — please complete cert rollout and confirm. Recommended follow-ups: coordinate rotations to avoid mixed fleets, increase jwks cache retention during rotations, and request signed exception if you want us to allow temporary mTLS bypass."
amina-cs: sent draft to customer. they acknowledged and said they'll finish rollout in ~25 minutes.
(25m later)
amina-cs: customer reports rollout complete at 03:58 UTC and all nodes report new cert and key present.
maria: monitoring shows errors drop to <0.1% for the last 5m. I'll flush hot-cache and restart bridge to pick up only the new key.
maria: flushing hot-cache and restarting. command: `sudo rm /var/lib/authbridge/hotcache/vectra.jwks && sudo systemctl restart redwood-auth-bridge`
maria: done. bridge logs: `hotcache removed tenant=vectra; runtime jwks refreshed keys=[be5b]`
(2m later)
alex: customer confirms full recovery. no further 401s.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-427 marked RESOLVED by maria. root cause: customer-initiated JWKS + client cert rotation causing mixed-key and expired cert state. mitigations: seeded hot-cache, CS coordination, implemented rotation-detection alert, auto-seed agent planned. follow-ups assigned to eng: create zero-downtime rotation playbook, extend jwks snapshot seeding, update runbook.
maria: adding postmortem action items: 1) playbook for customer-facing rotation (runbook owner: ben-eng) 2) alerting for jwks drift (owner: jordan) 3) document temporary mTLS bypass policy and exception flow (owner: sre-lead) 4) CS checklist for rotations (owner: amina-cs).
ben-eng: will own playbook, will prototype auto-seed script today and PR by EOD.
amina-cs: will follow up with customer exec summary and include recommended change window and checklist.
alex: thanks team. great coordination. :tada: 
sre-lead: adding one more note — for Private/VPC customers we should consider offering a managed key-rotation handoff option where we coordinate the JWKS swap so we never drop keys. I'll open an RFC.
maria: closing the thread. good job. :thumbsup:
